results.summary: Violence and tensions continue to escalate in various parts of the world, with Sudan's Kordofan region becoming the latest battleground between the Sudanese army and the RSF. In Ukraine, several people have been killed as Russian drones and missiles hit multiple cities, while in Nigeria, at least two people were killed and others kidnapped after gunmen attacked a church. The Israeli-Palestinian conflict also remains a major concern, with Israeli forces and settlers having killed 1,073 Palestinians in the occupied West Bank since October 2023, and Israeli attacks across Gaza having killed at least 69,513 Palestinians over the same period, according to reports. The Gaza Health Ministry has also reported that at least 280 Palestinians have been killed since a ceasefire started on October 10. Meanwhile, the US President has declared Saudi Arabia a major non-NATO ally after a visit from the Saudi Crown Prince, who announced plans to increase investment in the US to $1 trillion over four years, and the two countries have struck several deals, including the sale of US military jets. In other news, the US Congress has approved a bill forcing the Justice Department to release remaining Epstein files, and the US President has announced plans for a 'Gaza Board of Peace' that will include representatives from most major countries, which has been backed by a UN Security Council resolution. Additionally, China has banned all imports of Japanese seafood as a diplomatic dispute with Taiwan escalates, and Poland has closed the last operating Russian consulate in the city of Gdansk after a rail blast. In the Philippines, two cabinet ministers have resigned after being implicated in a corruption scandal, and in Indonesia, the alert level for Mount Semeru has been raised to the highest level after eruptions. Finally, Ukraine's president has attended peace talks, and the US and Saudi Arabia have strengthened their alliance, with the US President also commenting on the situation in Gaza.
